title: Part 8
html:
Indira Bai. The robber Naroji in the Chorananadi forest. Khandala, Nasik, Panchavati. Ashtabhuja and the sermon against animal sacrifice. The Tapti, Bharuch, Baroda, the death of Naroji. Ahmedabad (pp. 143–162)

[p. 143]

1560"I have grown old doing wicked deeds;
deliver me by giving me the dust of your feet."

1561Saying this, Indira rolled in the dust,
and the Lord delivered Indira by giving her the Name.

1562Having received the Name of Hari, the beautiful Indira
left her home, renouncing everything.

1563From that day all Khandoba's wives
became drunk with the Name of Hari, tears flowing from their eyes.

1564Never have I seen so merciful a Lord;
how many sinners he delivered — there is no counting them.

1565Having seen the muraris' devotion with his own eyes,
in the morning he wished to go to the Chorananadi forest.

1566The village people said, "What business have you there?
The Chorananadi forest is a mine of sin.

1567Many robbers live in the Chorananadi forest;
why do you wish to go there?"

1568The Lord said, "I will go to the Chorananadi forest;
seeing Chorananadi, my purpose will be fulfilled."

1569The village people said, "Do not go there, sannyasi;
we do not like holy men going there.

1570Great thieves and forest robbers live in that place;
if you go there your life will be in danger."

[p. 144]

1571The Lord said, "What can the robbers take from me?
I will go there right now."

1572Rama Svami said, "Lord, the Chorananadi forest
is no tirtha; what business have you there?

1573If the robbers do you some harm,
people will die of separation from you."

1574The Lord said, "Have no fear, Rama Svami;
I will make the robbers drunk with the Name of Hari."

1575Saying this, the Lord went to Chorananadi,
and arriving at Chorananadi he sat beneath a tree.

1576Here many wicked men have their den
and live by robbery.

1577A man came along saying "khai mai";
I could not understand anything he said.

1578The Lord, understanding all his speech,
answered him in "khai mai" and explained everything.

1579The man stood staring for a moment,
then, glancing this way and that, went back into the forest.

1580A very powerful man named Naroji
came forward with his weapons and arms.

1581Gradually two or four men appeared;
seeing the sannyasi, they all bowed down.

[p. 145]

1582Naroji said, "Come to my place;
you shall spend tonight there."

1583Hearing Naroji's words, the Lord said,
"I will pass tonight here beneath the tree."

1584Hearing the Lord's words, Naroji
told two or four men to bring alms.

1585Hearing Naroji's words, they all ran off,
and Nimai sat absorbed in the Name of Hari.

1586Some bring firewood and sugar, some rice,
some milk, some ghee, some fruits and roots.1

1587They brought heaps of food,
and seeing so much food my greed grew.

1588I had wandered through many lands with the Lord,
but nowhere had I seen so much food.

1589Having supplied all kinds of things and surrounding him on all sides,
Naroji's men stood in rows.

1590As he chanted the Name of Hari, my Lord
was then lost in love for Krishna.

1591Where was the milk and sugar, where the rice?
At the touch of his feet the fruits and roots were scattered.

1592Two or four men said, "What kind of sannyasi is this?
He spoils heaps of food on purpose."

[p. 146]

1593Naroji said, "I have never seen anything like it.
Why does my heart weep on seeing this sannyasi?

1594Who can tell how many sins I have committed?
Why today do I wish to put on a kaupina?

1595Why today does my heart weep?
Have I set my foot in the sannyasi's snare?

1596All the things are spoilt — have no fear;
I will bring all these things again."

1597Standing to one side, Naroji himself
gazed fixedly at Gora, the jewel of virtues.

1598Tears flowed from the Lord's eyes,
and everyone stood there like puppets.

1599Hearing of this, gradually the band of robbers
came out of the forest one by one.

1600In the afternoon my Gora, the jewel of virtues,
fainted with love and fell to the ground.

1601His body choked with love and grey with dust,
tears streaming down onto his breast.

1602Weeping, Naroji said, "Listen, sannyasi,
tell me plainly: what mantra have you recited?

1603Seeing your state, I think in my heart:
I will sin no more, living in this forest.

[p. 147]

1604I am sixty years old;
I will do no more sinful deeds, I will leave worldly life.

1605I, a brahmana's son, am a great villain;
do not hesitate to give me the dust of your feet.

1606I have no children and no household —
why then should I go on doing sinful deeds?

1607My belly will be fed if people give me alms;
why then should I stay with the robbers?

1608I have come to loathe evil deeds;
I will be chief of the robbers no longer."

1609Saying this, Naroji looked at his band
and at that moment threw down his weapons and arms.

1610The Lord said, "Naroji, listen to what I say;
how often must I tell you again and again?

1611Put on a kaupina and cover your nakedness;
feed yourself by begging and asking.

1612For whom do you hoard wealth?
Father, mother, brother, friend — no one belongs to anyone.

1613If a handful of rice keeps the body alive,
why hoard wealth sinfully?

1614Drink spring water from the cup of your hands;
what is the use of collecting many vessels?

[p. 148]

1615All the rich men equal to Kubera
will one day go to the city of the dead.

1616The road by which the poor man goes when he leaves this body
is the very road the emperor too must take.

1617Why die in vain, saying 'mine, mine'?
With love and devotion, brother, chant the Name of Hari."

1618Hearing this teaching, the brahmana Naroji
wished to come along with us.

1619Naroji said, "I will show you all the holy places;
from tirtha to tirtha I will follow you.

1620Until now my eyes were blinded by the smoke of delusion;
from today I have thrown my weapons to the ground.

1621With these hands I have committed so many murders,
with this mouth I have spoken so many harsh words.

1622I will be robber chief no longer.
What a path you have shown me, refuge of the helpless!

1623I always lived hidden in the jungle;
my body is riddled with sin, and I never gave it a thought."

1624Saying this, the robber chief gave up everything
and, putting on a kaupina, went with the Lord.

1625The robbers went off who knows where,
and Naroji came along with us.

[p. 149]

1626Then from the Chorananadi forest
the Lord set out to see Khandala.

1627The Mula river flows here, very swift;
arriving at Khandala, the Lord said to me:

1628"This river is a holy tirtha;
bathing here, sins are destroyed."

1629At the Lord's command I bathed
and went into the town to beg.

1630Naroji Thakura follows behind me;
having begged, I came back late in the day.

1631Gradually two or four people of Khandala
came and showed themselves to the Lord.

1632With pure hearts they all sat round about;
one said, "Come, Lord, to my estate."

1633All the people of Khandala are very hospitable;
they all tugged at him, eager to take him away.

1634At last they all started a quarrel
and were ready to come to blows.

1635One said, "I saw him first",
another said, "I brought the alms."

1636Thus they quarrelled with one another,
and seeing this my Lord laughed inwardly.

[p. 150]

1637A rich man said, "In my garden
I will give you alms today; go and stay there.

1638You have no cloth to wear — what a shame!
I wish to give you a piece of cloth.

1639If you want some money for the road,
whatever you ask, brother, I will bring at once."

1640Smiling, the Lord said, "Listen, maharaja,
I have no use for luxury or wealth.

1641I count even the torn cloth I wear as plenty;
I know I have no need of money.

1642Along with wealth, pride increases,
and with that pride the burden of sin grows.

1643This whole universe that you see with your eyes —
think where it will go.

1644All will become [illegible], all will be destroyed;
only the Lord of Brahma will remain.2

1645My two companions have brought alms;
what need is there of more alms?

1646The body must somehow be kept alive,
so on some days one has to take alms.

1647But tell me, what will come of a lot of food?
Give it to the poor and wretched and make up their want.

[p. 151]

1648Say 'Hari' with love, sitting beneath a tree,
and then you will all be able to cut your bonds.

1649There is no happiness in the bonds of maya;
with love and devotion say 'Hari' with your lips, brothers.

1650Love and devotion to God are made of rasa;
whoever knows them merges in the nectar of eternity.3

1651One who worships Krishna enjoys heaven forever;
for one who abandons Krishna there is hell."

1652Saying this, my Lord spoke no more
and, closing his eyes, began to sway.

1653Under the weight of his thrills his matted hair came loose,
his outer cloth slipped off and he began to dance.

1654Lost in love, his body grey with dust —
what can I say of love? To tell it would be a long story.

1655Chanting the Name of Hari, he passed the night sitting up,
and Naroji, sitting beside him, wiped away his sweat.

1656Rising in the morning, the Lord went to the town of Nasik
to make pilgrimage with a pure heart.

1657Here Thakura Lakshmana
cut off the nose of the rakshasi Shurpanakha.

1658To the west of it, near Tryambak,
is the site of Rama's hut.

[p. 152]

1659Going there, Mahaprabhu
offered hymns and praises and at last began kirtana.

1660"Rama's footprints are here" —
hearing this, he ran off into the forest.

1661In the depths of the dense forest, beside a spring,
two footprints stand out on a rock.

1662Touching the footprints,
he was overcome by a still deeper surge of love.

1663With his thrills, the matted locks on his head seemed to dance,
and his frail body seemed to swell.

1664The Lord said, "Where is Rama, lord of my life?
Show yourself lovingly and soothe my heart."

1665At last, clinging to my neck,
he burst into tears, saying, "Where is my Rama?"

1666The fragrance of lotus comes from the Lord's body,
and a breeze began to blow softly.

1667What can I say of love — I am afraid to speak of it;
never have I seen such a wondrous state.

1668At every turn he calls out, "O Krishna!"
and sometimes, like a madman, looks this way and that.

1669Who knows whom he calls, gazing at the sky;
sometimes he starts as though seeing something.

[p. 153]

1670A day or two pass in fasting;
from not eating, his body has grown thin.

1671Then, entering Panchavati,
he saw the Ganesha installed by Lakshmana.

1672One day, in a cave in the Panchavati forest,
coming back from begging, I secretly saw:

1673that deserted forest is utterly silent;
only now and then do two or four people live there.

1674The forest is ringing with stillness;
with closed eyes beautiful Gauranga is contemplating something.

1675A mass of radiance is coming forth from his body;
my young sannyasi is absorbed in meditation.

1676Seeing this state, my eyes were dazzled,
and I crept close to watch.

1677Naroji had gone somewhere to bring fruit;
I stood to one side.

1678Hearing footsteps, the Lord seemed suddenly,
before my very eyes, to restrain all his feelings.

1679Naroji, having gathered fruits and roots from somewhere,
stood before him with folded hands.

1680After making the offering and eating a little, Gora Raya
spent the whole night sitting up.

[p. 154]

1681Leaving Panchavati, my Gaura-Hari
went in the morning to the town of Daman.

1682He did not stay even a day in the town of Daman;
leaving Daman, the Lord went north.

1683Then for a fortnight, wandering and wandering,
Gora, the delight of hearts, spent his time on the road.

1684Gradually he came into the kingdom of Suratha4
and, seeing Ashtabhuja, lay rolling on the ground.

1685Having seen the eight-armed Bhagavati with his own eyes,
the Lord stayed there three days.

1686Ashtabhuja was installed by King Suratha;
seeing Bhagavati, he felt boundless joy.

1687In the goddess's temple there was a sannyasi;
he wished to ask the Lord something.

1688The sannyasi said, "Come, come, sannyasi gosai;
never have I seen a holy man like you.

1689Seeing you, devotion arises in my heart;
tell me, how shall I cross the ocean of worldly existence?

1690How should one worship the Supreme Lord?
Tell me this and remove my anxiety."

1691The Lord said, "I know no essential truth;
Bhavani will dispel all the darkness of your mind.

[p. 155]

1692As an ordinary heroine, seeing a handsome hero,
looks at him with her heart full of passion,5

1693in that same mood call on Krishna again and again,
and the darkness of your mind will vanish of itself."

1694While he was speaking, a brahmana
came to the goddess to sacrifice a goat.

1695The Lord said, "You make the sacrifice in order to eat it,
and do not know what your fate will be afterwards.

1696The goddess is a pure form — so the shastras say;
how could she eat what is forbidden?

1697King Suratha offered a hundred thousand sacrifices;
in the city of the dead a hundred thousand swords fall upon him.

1698You do not study the words of the shastras,
yet you practise religion by killing animals.

1699It was the meat-eating rakshasas who, in order to eat,
laid down the rule of killing animals.

1700Non-violence is the highest dharma, say all the shastras;
be kind to living beings and joy will arise.

1701Maya has bound you tightly;
how will you cut the bonds without a sword?

1702You crave tamasic food, and that is why
you are so eager to slaughter sheep and goats before the goddess.

[p. 156]

1703You think you will be saved by killing an animal,
and that is why you have come to make a sacrifice.

1704You can drive the soul out of the body,
but can you put the soul back into a dead body?

1705If someone before the goddess, with devotion,
were to cut off your head as a human sacrifice —

1706tell me, brother, how would your heart feel?
Let the animal go; I want to see it with my own eyes.

1707The eight-armed Bhagavati would eat wine and meat?
Hearing such a thing, a holy man would laugh it away.

1708Turn your minds to the eternal dharma
and, following the shastras, give up evil practices.

1709The goddess is a supreme Vaishnavi and does not eat meat;
why then do you try to beguile her with sacrifices?

1710If killing living beings were dharma,
why are robbers not called holy men?

1711The fisherman kills many fish every day —
why should I not call him righteous?

1712Killing men and killing animals are great sins;
if you commit this sin, the threefold misery will increase."

1713Going to see the eight-armed Bhagavati,
he gave this teaching, examining the shastras.

[p. 157]

1714The man who had come to worship Durga
listened to the Lord's words with devotion.

1715Hearing the Lord's words, he became detached,
and the brahmana let the sacrificial goat go.

1716Worshipping with flowers and bilva leaves, the excellent brahmana
went back home happily.

1717The Lord sat down firmly before the goddess
and with folded hands began a hymn to Bhavani.

1718Having offered praise and obeisance to Bhavani, Gora Raya
hurried towards the river Tapti, a great tirtha.

1719Bathing three times a day in the waters of the Tapti,
he went to see the image of Vamana.

1720On an open plain near the Tapti
an image of Lord Vamana is installed.

1721King Bali installed this image;
for this reason the Tapti became a tirtha.

1722Vamana bathed in the waters of the Tapti,
and that is why the Tapti is called a great tirtha.

1723Having bowed at the feet of Lord Vamana,
Gaura-Hari went to see the sacrificial pit.

1724To see the sacrificial pit in the town of Bharoch,
he left the Tapti and went to the bank of the Narmada.

[p. 158]

1725In Bharoch King Bali performed sacrifice at a sacrificial pit;
he goes with a joyful heart to see it.

1726Seeing with his own eyes the huge hollow of the pit,
boundless joy arose in Chaitanya's heart.

1727Having bathed in the Narmada, a great tirtha,
Gora, the delight of hearts, went to the town of Baroda.

1728East of Baroda is Thakura Dakorji;6
the Lord wished to see Dakorji.

1729In Dakorji's courtyard there is a huge tamala tree,
and beneath it the darling of Shachi stood.

1730Having seen Dakorji, the Lord offered obeisance and praise
and came back again to the town of Baroda.

1731The king of Baroda is very virtuous;
the worthy king is devoted to the service of Govinda.

1732With his own hands he sweeps Govinda's temple;
people say to one another that the king is like Ambarisha.

1733The maharaja is always busy for Govinda's sake;
the king is always full of love for Govinda's service.

1734Gathering tulasi with his own hands,
the king offers it at Govinda's lotus feet with devotion.

1735In the evening Gora goes to Govinda's house
and, seeing Govinda, rolls on the ground in love.

[p. 159]

1736A single torn outer cloth, the look of a madman;
the Lord is always intoxicated, absorbed in Krishna.

1737His whole body smeared with dust, his eyes closed;
seeing Govinda, he sheds tears.

1738After three days a calamity occurred here:
Naroji died of fever.

1739At the time of death Gora Raya sat before him
and stroked Naroji's body with his lotus hand.

1740When Naroji closed his eyes,
he himself gave Krishna's name into his ear from his holy lips.

1741Naroji Thakura is very fortunate:
Bhagavan gave Krishna's name into his ear.

1742At the time of death Naroji, with folded hands,
looking towards the Lord, said "Hari, Hari".

1743Taking Naroji in his arms, Lord Vishvambhara
moved him from beneath the tamala tree.

1744Having begged [what was needed], Naroji was buried,
and the Lord performed kirtana circling the grave.

1745The maharaja, hearing of this by word of mouth,
came himself with a crowd to see the sannyasi.

1746Seeing the Lord, the king bowed down,
and the Lord said nothing, good or bad.

[p. 160]

1747Respectfully the king invited him to take alms.
The Lord said, "I take alms at householders' doors.

1748I have no need of alms of luxury;
that is why I do not ask alms at your door."

1749With folded hands the king asked him to accept alms,
and, having no choice, he told me to accept them.

1750At the Lord's sign, from the king,
like an ordinary man, I begged a handful of alms.

1751Having given alms, the maharaja went away,
and Gora-chand completed his daily rites.

1752Rising in the morning, we go westwards
and, going a little way, reach the Mahanadi.7

1753A very swift river, beautiful to see,
with many stones rushing along in it.

1754Crossing the river, my Gora, the delight of hearts,
reached the vicinity of Ahmedabad.

1755Wondrous Ahmedabad, a splendid city:
how many gardens, how many charming houses!

1756Huge mansions stand in splendour in its midst;
the people of the country are always devoted to serving guests.

1757The village people regard a guest as equal to a god
and serve guests with all their hearts.

[p. 161]

1758Enchanted by the Lord's beauty, people
came with devotion and stood all around.

1759Some said, "Listen, listen, young sannyasi,
come to my house; I will give you alms and serve you."

1760The Lord said, "I will not go to a householder's home;
tonight I will stay by the Nandani."

1761There is a beautiful garden called Nandani;
at its edge Lord Vishvambhara settled down.

1762Seeing this, the village people brought alms,
and at night Gora-chand made the offering.

1763Many people came and surrounded the Lord
and, seeing the sannyasi, spoke with devotion.

1764A pandit came and showed himself
and began to recite verses of the Srimad-Bhagavata.

1765The Lord said, "Sing Krishna's glories well;
I wish to forget everything while hearing the verses.

1766You study the Bhagavata every day;
seeing you, the torment of worldly life goes away.

1767Every day you sing the glories of Krishna;
blessed, blessed are you, brahmana, you are most fortunate."

1768Having talked with the Lord, the brahmana
called all the people and said:

[p. 162]

1769"All of you serve this sannyasi well;
this sannyasi is no ordinary man — he must be some god.

1770Seeing him, detachment arises;
know for certain he is no ordinary man."

1771I cannot understand all the speech of the people;
what I can, I write down from gestures and hints.

1772Having long travelled the tirthas of this country,
Shachi's darling understands everyone's speech.

1773Sometimes, asking the Lord about a word or two,
I write it down in my karcha after thinking it over.

1774The lila that I have seen with my own eyes
I record in my karcha very secretly.8

1775Always intoxicated, the Lord, in an ecstasy of love for Krishna,
wanders from tirtha to tirtha, from land to land.

1776In Ahmedabad many people gathered;
they all come in crowds to see the Lord.

1777Seeing many people all around, Gora Raya,
drunk with joy, distributes the Name to all.

1778The Lord said, "With devotion all of you chant the Name;
all suffering will go far away and no sorrow will remain.

1779Do not despise anyone out of pride;
free from pride, say 'Hare Krishna Hare'."

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. D. C. Sen quotes this couplet in his introduction as evidence in the dispute over whether Chaitanya ate rice (ata-chuna).
  2. The line is badly corrupted in the edition; the translation is approximate.
  3. The line is partly corrupted; translated from the sense.
  4. The edition reads "Harather rajya", apparently "the kingdom of Suratha" (cf. below, "Suratha installed Ashtabhuja").
  5. Ragatmika, "full of passion (raga)", a term of the Gaudiya Vaishnava theory of spontaneous devotion.
  6. Dakorji is Ranchhodrai at Dakor (Gujarat), a famous deity of Krishna.
  7. Probably the river Mahi (Gujarat).
  8. Another statement by the author, key for the whole book, about how he kept his notes.
